title: Corporate Wellness Partnership: re-enrollment cooldown after a prior enrollment is closed
content:
Under the Corporate Wellness Partnership, an employee whose prior corporate wellness enrollment was closed may re-enroll only when the new tier's re-enrollment setting permits re-enrollment after removal, and only once the new tier's re-enrollment cooldown has elapsed.

The cooldown clock starts from the date the employee's prior corporate wellness enrollment record shows as closed — the verifiable business record of that closure, correlated to that same employee. It is counted forward in full calendar days from that closed date, with no partial-day rounding, for the number of calendar days the new tier sets as its re-enrollment cooldown. The moment the employee gives notice of wanting to re-enroll must not be earlier than that closed date plus the cooldown period; reaching that boundary day itself already satisfies the cooldown, and a day before it does not.

Where the new tier's re-enrollment setting does not permit re-enrollment after removal, the employee may not re-enroll under that tier regardless of how much time has passed since the prior enrollment closed.

Boundary example (a hypothetical cooldown length, not any tier's actual figure): where a cooldown period runs for a chosen number of calendar days from the closed date, notice of re-enrollment given exactly on the day that period is reached already satisfies the cooldown; notice given one calendar day earlier does not, because the full period has not yet elapsed.

Whether re-enrollment is permitted after removal, and the length of the cooldown, both vary by partnership tier and are stated in a separate document.
